purpose: Ezetimibe is used to lower your LDL cholesterol, often called 'bad' cholesterol. It is used along with a healthy diet and sometimes with other cholesterol-lowering medicines. Keeping your cholesterol under control helps protect your heart and reduce your risk of heart attack or stroke.
how_it_works: Your small intestine normally absorbs cholesterol from the food you eat and lets it enter your bloodstream. Ezetimibe works by blocking a protein in your intestine that acts like a door for cholesterol, keeping much of it from getting into your blood. This means less bad cholesterol ends up circulating in your body.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medicine well. Some people may notice mild stomach upset, diarrhea, or stomach pain. You might also experience muscle aches, tiredness, or a runny nose. These side effects are usually mild and often go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have unusual muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially if you also take a statin medication, as there is a small risk of a serious muscle problem. Let your doctor know if you have liver problems before starting this medicine. Avoid taking ezetimibe if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without first talking to your doctor. Always tell your pharmacist about all other medicines and supplements you take.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 10 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. You can take it at any time of day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
